scope: PT2491: six new original model PNGs compared directly with all historical raster references listed in their input specs; principal masses, silhouette, roof hierarchy and major openings. Small ornament may remain approximate.
evidencePolicy: Actual PNGs and historical raster views are evidence. Producer prose, prompts and prior candidates are not treated as proof of historical agreement. Input specs used to identify references only.
decision: No unambiguous principal-mass FAIL established in the supplied views. Three visual matches pass with reconstruction caveats; Trocadero proportions, Haring lower-belfry enclosure and townhall right-gable silhouette retain explicit warnings. This independent visual report grants no owner or Tripo approval.

items.summary: The substantial two-level side gallery reaches approximately the main roof spring/eave, visually around half the main hall height; the former tiny-gallery/high-exposed-wall error is absent. The low pointed great roof, glazed pointed end and long repeated-bay hall are recognizable.
warnings: The separate gallery roof is interpreted with a shallow outward slope rather than the nearly flat platform-like section drawn in M3; exact gallery depth and hidden far-side/rear junction cannot be certified from this image.
Exact bay counts, glazing divisions and fine iron ornament are approximate and nonblocking for principal-mass comparison.
decisiveEvidence: M3 transverse section shows two-level outboard gallery reaching the great arch spring, about half the ridge height.
M1 corroborates the pointed glazed end, iron truss and fan glazing.
M2 corroborates the long rectangular repeated-bay footprint.

items.summary: The whole palace now includes both long low curved wings and both terminal pavilions. Twin towers, articulated central hall, arcaded projecting front and roof hierarchy agree broadly with T1/T3/T4. Central-to-total apparent span remains a proportion caveat.

materialIssues.issue: The central assembly still appears broader relative to the total palace span than in the distant T3 photograph.
materialIssues.basis: Direct visual comparison of the generated palace and T3; the side pavilions around the central rotunda occupy a visibly larger share of the rendered span.
materialIssues.limitation: This is an apparent image-space difference, not a verified dimension error. T3 and the render differ in camera distance/elevation and the wings and central facade occupy different footprint depths. Perspective and the curved-wing depth can plausibly explain a substantial part of the discrepancy; no measured footprint plan is supplied. A greater-than-15-percent physical discrepancy is not established.

warnings: Wing curve depth, rear volume and exact footprint remain reconstruction judgments; T4 is a transverse section, not a footprint plan.
Fine tower/arcade ornament is approximate and is not a blocking criterion.
decisiveEvidence: T3 supplies the complete broad palace span and both low wings.
T1 supplies the projecting lower arcade and central hall/tower forms.
T4 supplies the central section roof and height hierarchy only.

items.summary: The long low transverse palace has a narrow modest central dome, lower inner connecting ranges, raised intermediate pavilions and articulated outer ranges. The oversize-central-dome failure is absent; overall pavilion/roof rhythm agrees with U1.
warnings: U1 partially obscures/crops terminal extents behind the foreground Louvre blocks, so the isolated end faces and precise total end extent are inferred.
U2 is an earlier unmeasured context plan; U3 supplies only a distant garden silhouette. Hidden garden elevation, roof joins and repeated window details remain approximate.
Minor dormer/chimney/stone ornament differences are nonblocking for the requested mass-and-silhouette scope.
decisiveEvidence: U1 decisive far-background palace range shows the modest dome, low connectors and raised intermediate pavilion rhythm.
U2 identifies the intended transverse range A, rather than the perpendicular Louvre galleries.
U3 corroborates only the modest central dome silhouette.

items.summary: Broad faceted masonry shaft and successively narrower clock/belfry/lantern assembly follow H2. The corrected order is visible: belfry, balustraded collar, inward-curved transition, upper open lantern, curved cap and fish vane.

materialIssues.issue: The lower belfry is open through most of its height, exposing the bell and framing; H2 shows arched upper apertures above a lower panelled/solid zone with separate rectangular articulation.
materialIssues.basis: Compare the rendered stage immediately above the clock with H2 elevation D; H4 also suggests a darker lower enclosed portion.
materialIssues.limitation: Exact historical-phase openings and materials are less secure across H2 versus H3/H4; this is a meaningful opening-treatment warning, not a claim of measured dimensional failure.

warnings: Fine mouldings, finials, clocks and rear masonry openings remain interpreted.
H2 is a later documented profile than the harbour scenes; phase consistency is limited.
decisiveEvidence: H2 controls stage order, relative widths and elevation/profile.
H1 controls only the faceted tower footprint.
H3 and H4 corroborate the broad shaft and narrowing upper silhouette.

items.summary: The three round/segmental ground openings, three-window upper hall, steep hipped roof, narrow square civic tower and long receding compound ranges match the principal T2/T3 composition. The former pointed opening/church-belfry type errors are absent.

materialIssues.issue: The right civic-range gable is rendered as a conspicuous stair-step gable. T2 lower drawing and T3 instead show a predominantly sloping triangular/shouldered gable profile.
materialIssues.basis: Direct comparison of the large right-hand gable in both historical views with the generated right-hand range.
materialIssues.limitation: Small shoulders and ornamental projections are ambiguous in the sources, but the generated multi-step staircase is a stronger silhouette treatment than the rasters support. The prompt describing a stepped gable is not historical evidence.

warnings: T2 and T3 may share a source tradition; they are not guaranteed independent corroboration.
The irregular plan T1 does not fully certify the rendered rear roof joins or long side-window rhythm.
Small carved/brick ornament and window subdivisions are approximate and nonblocking.
decisiveEvidence: T3 is the clearest front/side massing view and shows broad round ground openings beneath decorative curves.
T2 lower drawing corroborates the arcade, hipped hall, narrow tower and right-hand sloping gable.
T1 documents the accumulated irregular compound footprint rather than a symmetrical palace.

items.summary: The front has the correct two central round fluted Doric columns and two square outer piers, three tall rectangular openings, deep horizontal entablature and shallow triangular pediment. The tall support-to-width and pediment/entablature hierarchy are plausible against both photographs.
warnings: E1 is a stereo duplication of one viewpoint, not two independent views. E2 is low resolution.
Rear supports, roof back and exact portico depth are inferred; the render visibly includes rear support geometry that the frontal source set cannot independently certify.
Fluting, triglyph/moulding and inscription details are approximate and nonblocking.
decisiveEvidence: E1 shows two round fluted central shafts, square outer piers and tall rectangular passage openings.
E2 corroborates the high-support profile and shallow pediment in a slightly different view.
